{{short description|American biostatistician}}
'''Margaret Merrell''' (December 3, 1900<ref>''Cook County, Illinois, Birth Certificates Index, 1871-1922''</ref> – 21, 1995){{r|glob}} was an American [[biostatistician]] who taught at [[Johns Hopkins University]] for many years{{r|jhu1}} and became the first female full professor in the [[Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health|Johns Hopkins School of Public Health]].{{r|thomas}} She is known for her research with [[Lowell Reed]] on the construction of [[life table]]s.{{r|jhu1|ltt}} She also observed that, for [[longitudinal data]] on individuals, fitting a curve to each individual and then averaging the parameters describing the curve will typically give different results than averaging the data values of the individuals and fitting a single curve to the averaged data.{{r|tanner}}

==Biography==
Merrell was born in [[La Grange, Illinois]].{{r|glob}} She entered [[Wellesley College]] as an honor student from [[Framingham High School]],{{r|welhon}} and became vice-president of the Wellesley mathematics club.{{r|amm}} She graduated in 1922, and took a position as a schoolteacher in [[Baltimore]].{{r|jhu2}} She joined Johns Hopkins as an instructor and graduate student in 1925, and completed her [[Sc.D.]] there in 1930.{{r|jhu1}} Her dissertation, supervised by Lowell Reed, was ''The Relationship of Individual Growth to Average Growth''.{{r|mgp}}

After completing her doctorate, Merrell remained on the Johns Hopkins faculty.{{r|jhu1}} During [[World War II]], she consulted with the U.S. Army on treatments for [[sexually transmitted disease]]s and for [[motion sickness]].{{r|jhu2}} As a faculty member at Johns Hopkins, she "reportedly carried most of her department's teaching load"{{r|rossiter}} and was described as "the intellectual power behind the throne" of the department.{{r|jhu1}} She was promoted to full professor in 1957,{{r|thomas}} served as acting chair of biostatistics in 1957–1958, and retired in 1959.{{r|jhu1|thomas}}

She died in 1995, in a nursing home in [[Berlin, New Hampshire]].{{r|glob}}

==Honors and awards==
Merrell was honored by the [[American Statistical Association]] in 1951 by election as a fellow of the association.{{r|fasa}}

The Helen Abbey and Margaret Merrell Professorship in Biostatistics Education at [[Johns Hopkins University]] is named after her and Professor [[Helen Abbey]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Helen Abbey and Margaret Merrell Professorship in Biostatistics Education |url=https://professorships.jhu.edu/professorship/helen-abbey-and-margaret-merrell-professorship-in-biostatistical-education/ |website=Johns Hopkins University |date=23 June 2016 |accessdate=15 March 2020}}</ref>
